You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2025 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 24(b) [3 marks]: Employees at a factory have been discouraged by their employers from joining a union.
Explain TWO possible reasons for this.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 3):
3 marks: Explains TWO possible reasons for employers discouraging employees from joining a union
2 marks: Outlines TWO possible reasons OR | Explains ONE possible reason
1 marks: Provides some relevant information

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Unions will advocate for higher pay and better conditions like leave and work health and safety processes. These changes are costly and will reduce the profits of the business.
Employers may also discourage unionisation as it brings their processes under further scrutiny which could lead to fines, staff turnover and industrial action which is also costly.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: use examples of technology impacting human resources
Better responses: provide two reasons an employer may discourage their employees from joining a union, and the impact of each
Better responses: demonstrate knowledge of how the practices outlined in the stimulus were illegal
Better responses: integrate relevant legal concepts to show the impacts of the illegal practices.
To improve: demonstrating understanding of the key words in the question
To improve: making clear links between the illegal practices identified and the effects on human resources
To improve: showing an understanding of the current legal framework relevant to human resources.

STUDENT RESPONSE:
"""

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-3>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '3'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a full-mark answer in 2 to 5 plain sentences a student could realistically write in the exam>"}
